# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Doodnaught_2017_buprenorphine_cat"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Doodnaught_2017_buprenorphine_cat"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0176443> (open access; the
  model is described in S3 File, Appendix 3, and the individual data are in
  S4 File).

Doodnaught et al. gave a high-concentration buprenorphine formulation
(Simbadol, 1.8 mg/mL) to six conscious cats by three routes in a crossover
design and fitted one joint population model in Phoenix NLME to plasma
buprenorphine and norbuprenorphine from all routes at once. The
pharmacodynamic model for the thermal threshold was then fitted
sequentially with the PK parameters held at their estimates.

Structure (Figure 2 of the paper):

* **Buprenorphine** -- two compartments (CL, V1, CL2, V2), shared by all
  routes; doses and parameters are per kg body weight.
* **Buccal (OTM) route** -- first-order absorption (kaOTM) with
  bioavailability FOTM.
* **Subcutaneous route** -- total bioavailability FSC split between an
  inverse-Gaussian input (fraction BIO; mean input time MAT and relative
  dispersion CV, S3 File eq 5) giving a sharp peak at about 5 minutes, and a
  time-dependent first-order input (the remaining 1 - BIO) whose rate
  constant rises logistically to kaSC with half-time T50 and a shape
  parameter set equal to CL (S3 File eq 7).
* **Norbuprenorphine** -- two compartments, formed from central
  buprenorphine at the first-order rate KaMet; after a buccal dose it also
  enters from a gut-norbuprenorphine (first-pass) depot at rate
  Kafirst-pass.
* **Thermal threshold** -- effect compartment (Ke0) driving a sigmoid Emax
  model on top of a baseline T0 (equation 1).

# Population

Six healthy adult domestic short-haired cats (four males, two females; body
weight 4.9 +/- 0.7 kg) from the Universite de Montreal received, in random
order with at least 14 days of washout, Simbadol 0.12 mg/kg i.v., 0.24 mg/kg
s.c. and 0.12 mg/kg buccally (Methods 'Animals' and 'Experimental design').
Plasma was sampled from a jugular central venous catheter at 2 and 8 min and
at 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 30, 36, 48, 60 and 72 h; the thermal threshold
was measured at the same times from 0.5 h. A saline arm (Phase I) gave
thermal thresholds only.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Doodnaught_2017_buprenorphine_cat")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every value is from the Results section of the paper unless stated; IIV
percentages are converted with S3 File eq 3, omega^2 = log(CV^2 + 1).

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(0.98) L/kg/h, IIV 2.4% | Results 'Pharmacokinetic modeling and parameters' |
| `lvc` (V1) | log(0.75) L/kg, IIV 11.3% | same paragraph |
| `lq` (CL2) | log(0.70) L/kg/h, IIV 0% (no eta) | same paragraph |
| `lvp` (V2) | log(7.15) L/kg, IIV 8.1% | same paragraph |
| `logitfdepot_buccal` (FOTM) | logit(0.236), IIV 25% | OTM paragraph; logit scale per S3 File eq 2 |
| `lka_buccal` (kaOTM) | log(1.67) 1/h, IIV 25.1% | OTM paragraph |
| `logitfdepot_sc` (FSC) | logit(0.94), IIV 23.4% | SC paragraph |
| `logitfrel` (BIO) | logit(0.101), IIV 113% | SC paragraph |
| `lmat_invgauss` (MAT) | log(7.21) h, IIV 3.5% | SC paragraph; Figure 2 legend |
| `lcv_invgauss` (CV) | log(5.46), IIV 0.5% | SC paragraph |
| `lka_sc` (kaSC) | log(0.062) 1/h, IIV 14.9% | SC paragraph |
| `lka_t50` (T50) | log(2.8) h, IIV 27% | SC paragraph |
| `lkmet` (KaMet) | fixed(log(0.196)) 1/h, IIV 19% | norbuprenorphine paragraph ('then fixed') |
| `lka_norbup` (Kafirst-pass) | log(0.626) 1/h, IIV 6.9% | norbuprenorphine paragraph |
| `lcl_norbup` (CLMet) | log(0.42) L/kg/h, IIV 4.3% | norbuprenorphine paragraph |
| `lvc_norbup` (V1Met) | log(0.323) L/kg, IIV 0.1% | norbuprenorphine paragraph |
| `lq_norbup` (CL2Met) | log(7.662) L/kg/h, no eta | norbuprenorphine paragraph ('not estimated') |
| `lvp_norbup` (V2Met) | log(4.69) L/kg, no eta | norbuprenorphine paragraph |
| `lke0` (Ke0) | log(0.52) 1/h, IIV 0% | Results 'PK-PD modeling' |
| `le0` (T0) | log(46.1) degrees C, IIV 0% | Results 'PK-PD modeling' |
| `lemax` (Emax) | log(5.62) degrees C, IIV 0% | Results 'PK-PD modeling' |
| `lec50` (EC50) | log(2.13) ng/mL, IIV 447% | Results 'PK-PD modeling' |
| `lhill` (n) | log(1.54), IIV 91% | Results 'PK-PD modeling' |
| `propSd`, `propSd_norbup`, `addSd_thermal_threshold` | fixed(0) | error models named (Figure 2; S3 File Table 2) but magnitudes not reported |
| inverse-Gaussian input | n/a | S3 File eq 5; mode from eq 6 |
| time-dependent input, gamma = CL | n/a | S3 File eq 7 and the sentence after it |
| norbuprenorphine formation and first-pass depot | n/a | Figure 2; norbuprenorphine paragraph |
| `d/dt(effect)`, sigmoid Emax | n/a | S3 File eq 8; equation 1 (S3 File eq 9) |

# Derived quantities reported in the paper

These are computed from the packaged parameters and must agree with the
secondary values the paper prints.

```{r derived}
mod <- readModelDb("Doodnaught_2017_buprenorphine_cat")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
th <- ui$theta

cl <- exp(th[["lcl"]]); vc <- exp(th[["lvc"]]); q <- exp(th[["lq"]]); vp <- exp(th[["lvp"]])
k10 <- cl / vc; k12 <- q / vc; k21 <- q / vp
beta <- ((k10 + k12 + k21) - sqrt((k10 + k12 + k21)^2 - 4 * k10 * k21)) / 2
mat <- exp(th[["lmat_invgauss"]]); cvig <- exp(th[["lcv_invgauss"]])

derived <- tibble::tribble(
  ~quantity, ~paper, ~model,
  "Vdss = V1 + V2 (L/kg)", 7.89, vc + vp,
  "Beta half-life (h)", 12.3, log(2) / beta,
  "Mode of the inverse-Gaussian input (h)", 0.08,
    mat * (sqrt(1 + 9 / 4 * cvig^4) - 3 / 2 * cvig^2),
  "Buccal absorption half-life (h)", 0.42, log(2) / exp(th[["lka_buccal"]]),
  "Late SC absorption half-life at kaSC (h)", 11.2, log(2) / exp(th[["lka_sc"]]),
  "KaMet transformation half-life (h)", 3.5, log(2) / exp(th[["lkmet"]]),
  "First-pass norbuprenorphine absorption half-life (h)", 1.1, log(2) / exp(th[["lka_norbup"]])
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - paper) / paper)

knitr::kable(derived, digits = 3, caption = "Secondary quantities: paper vs packaged model.")

# The paper rounds each quantity to two or three significant figures. The
# inverse-Gaussian mode is printed to one significant figure (0.08 h), so its
# tolerance is the half-unit of that last digit.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(derived$pct_diff[-3]) < 3),
  abs(derived$model[3] - 0.08) < 0.005
)
```

The mode check fixes the meaning of the printed CV: with CV = 5.46 entered
squared in equation 5 the input peaks at 0.081 h, matching the paper's
'initial peak of plasma concentration observed at 0.08 hours'. Reading 5.46
as CV^2 instead would put the peak at 0.44 h.

A buccal dose is entered as two records of the same amount, one into
`depot_buccal` and one into `depot_norbup`: the model applies FOTM to both,
as the paper's 'FOTM (parent and metabolite OTM bioavailability)'
describes. Observation rows carry `dvid = 1` because the model has three
outputs.

```{r events}
route_dose <- c(IV = 0.12, OTM = 0.12, SC = 0.24)  # mg/kg

make_route <- function(route, ids, times) {
  dose_cmt <- switch(route,
    IV = "central",
    OTM = c("depot_buccal", "depot_norbup"),
    SC = "depot_sc"
  )
  doses <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, cmt = dose_cmt) |>
    mutate(time = 0, amt = route_dose[[route]], evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    mutate(cmt = NA_character_, amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(route = route) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

sample_times <- sort(unique(c(0, obs_pk$time)))
plot_times <- sort(unique(c(sample_times, seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 60), seq(1, 72, by = 0.25))))

ev_typ <- bind_rows(
  make_route("IV", 1L, plot_times),
  make_route("OTM", 2L, plot_times),
  make_route("SC", 3L, plot_times)
)

mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "route",
                           atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 1 of Doodnaught 2017 (mean +/- SD plasma concentrations),
# with the typical-value prediction as the line.
typ_long <- sim_typ |>
  select(route, time, buprenorphine = Cc, norbuprenorphine = Cc_norbup) |>
  pivot_longer(c(buprenorphine, norbuprenorphine), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")
# Log axis: drop the pre-dose point and the BLQ zeros from the plots only.
typ_long <- typ_long[typ_long$time > 0, ]
obs_long <- obs_pk |>
  select(route, time, buprenorphine = bup, norbuprenorphine = nor) |>
  pivot_longer(c(buprenorphine, norbuprenorphine), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc")
obs_long <- obs_long[obs_long$conc > 0, ]

ggplot(typ_long, aes(time, conc, colour = route)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = obs_long) +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)", colour = "Route",
       caption = "Lines: typical-value prediction. Points: mean of six cats (S4 File).\nReplicates Figure 1 of Doodnaught 2017.")
```

```{r figure-1-check}
pk_cmp <- sim_typ |>
  mutate(tmin = round(time * 60)) |>
  select(route, tmin, Cc, Cc_norbup) |>
  inner_join(obs_pk, by = c("route", "tmin")) |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 0.5)

fit_summary <- pk_cmp[pk_cmp$nor > 0, ] |>
  group_by(route) |>
  summarise(median_abs_log_ratio_nor = median(abs(log(Cc_norbup / nor))), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    pk_cmp |> group_by(route) |>
      summarise(median_abs_log_ratio_bup = median(abs(log(Cc / bup))), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "route"
  )
knitr::kable(fit_summary, digits = 3,
             caption = "Median |log(typical prediction / observed mean)| from 0.5 h on.")

peak_nor_otm <- c(
  model = max(sim_typ$Cc_norbup[sim_typ$route == "OTM"]),
  observed = max(obs_pk$nor[obs_pk$route == "OTM"])
)
peak_nor_otm

stopifnot(
  # Buprenorphine: the typical curve tracks the mean data within about 20%
  # at the median time point for every route (realised 0.08-0.19).
  all(fit_summary$median_abs_log_ratio_bup < log(1.5)),
  # Norbuprenorphine after IV and SC (realised 0.15 and 0.42).
  all(fit_summary$median_abs_log_ratio_nor[fit_summary$route != "OTM"] < log(2)),
  # Buccal norbuprenorphine peak: FOTM applied to the first-pass depot gives
  # 4.4 ng/mL against an observed 4.2 ng/mL; a first-pass fraction of 1% of
  # the dose would give about 0.6 ng/mL.
  abs(log(peak_nor_otm[["model"]] / peak_nor_otm[["observed"]])) < log(1.3)
)
```

The buccal norbuprenorphine curve peaks at the observed height but at about
4 h instead of 1 h, and stays about twice the observed mean from 4 to 48 h;
see Assumptions and deviations.

## Bioavailability and clearance by mass balance

With the typical values, `CL x AUC(0-inf) / dose` must return 1 for the
i.v. dose, FSC = 0.94 for s.c. and FOTM = 0.236 for buccal. This checks that
the two SC inputs together deliver exactly FSC of the dose (the
inverse-Gaussian density integrates to 1) and that the buccal first-pass
depot does not leak buprenorphine.

```{r mass-balance}
mb_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 1, by = 1 / 120), seq(1, 24, by = 0.1), seq(24, 600, by = 1))))
ev_mb <- bind_rows(
  make_route("IV", 1L, mb_times),
  make_route("OTM", 2L, mb_times),
  make_route("SC", 3L, mb_times)
)
sim_mb <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_mb, keep = "route",
                          atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12, hmax = 0.01, maxsteps = 1e6) |>
  as.data.frame()

auc_trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)
mb <- sim_mb |>
  group_by(route) |>
  summarise(auc = auc_trap(time, Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    dose = route_dose[route],
    f_model = cl * auc / 1000 / dose,
    f_paper = c(IV = 1, OTM = 0.236, SC = 0.94)[route]
  )
knitr::kable(mb, digits = 4, caption = "CL x AUC / dose against the published bioavailability.")
stopifnot(all(abs(mb$f_model / mb$f_paper - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Virtual cohort and simulation

The stochastic simulation uses 200 virtual cats per route. No covariates
enter the model (all parameters are per kg). The residual errors are fixed to
zero because the paper does not report their magnitudes, so the bands show
between-cat variability only.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2017)
n_per_route <- 200L
events <- bind_rows(
  make_route("IV", seq_len(n_per_route), sample_times),
  make_route("OTM", n_per_route + seq_len(n_per_route), sample_times),
  make_route("SC", 2L * n_per_route + seq_len(n_per_route), sample_times)
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid", "cmt")])))

sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, keep = "route") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-s5, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates the stratified VPCs of S3 File (Fig suppl. 5a-f) in summary form.
vpc <- sim |>
  select(id, route, time, buprenorphine = Cc, norbuprenorphine = Cc_norbup)
vpc <- vpc[vpc$time > 0, ] |>
  pivot_longer(c(buprenorphine, norbuprenorphine), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  group_by(route, analyte, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), q50 = median(conc), q95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = obs_long, aes(y = conc), colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_grid(analyte ~ route, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Plasma concentration (ng/mL)",
       caption = "Median and 90% interval of 200 virtual cats per route; points: observed means.\nReplicates Fig suppl. 5a-f of S3 File.")
```

```{r figure-s10}
# Replicates the pharmacodynamic VPCs of S3 File (Fig suppl. 10a-c) and the
# means of Table 2.
tt_vpc <- sim |>
  group_by(route, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(thermal_threshold, 0.05),
    q50 = median(thermal_threshold),
    q95 = quantile(thermal_threshold, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(tt_vpc, aes(time, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(data = sim_typ, aes(y = thermal_threshold), linetype = 2) +
  geom_point(data = obs_tt, aes(y = TT), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 55, linetype = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~route) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Thermal threshold (degrees C)",
       caption = "Solid: median of 200 virtual cats per route; dashed: typical value;\npoints: Table 2 means; dotted: 55 degrees C safety cut-off.")
```

```{r pd-check}
pd_cmp <- sim_typ |>
  select(route, time, thermal_threshold) |>
  inner_join(obs_tt, by = c("route", "time"))
pd_summary <- pd_cmp |>
  group_by(route) |>
  summarise(median_abs_diff_C = median(abs(thermal_threshold - TT)), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(pd_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "Median |typical prediction - Table 2 mean| (degrees C).")
stopifnot(
  # Realised 0.6-1.2 degrees C; Table 2 SDs are 1-5 degrees C.
  all(pd_summary$median_abs_diff_C < 2),
  # Baseline before dosing is T0 for every route.
  all(abs(sim_typ$thermal_threshold[sim_typ$time == 0] - 46.1) < 1e-6)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA of the simulated buprenorphine and norbuprenorphine profiles at the
study's sampling times, per route.

```{r pknca}
# PKNCAdose() reserves the argument name `route`, so the grouping column is
# called `treatment` here.
nca_one <- function(sim, conc_col) {
  conc <- sim |>
    select(id, treatment = route, time, conc = all_of(conc_col)) |>
    filter(!is.na(conc))
  conc <- bind_rows(conc, conc |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, conc = 0)) |>
    distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(id, treatment, time)
  # One dose row per cat: the second buccal record (into depot_norbup) is the
  # same administration.
  doses <- events |>
    filter(evid == 1, cmt != "depot_norbup") |>
    mutate(dose_route = ifelse(route == "IV", "intravascular", "extravascular")) |>
    select(id, treatment = route, time, amt, dose_route)
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | treatment + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + id, route = "dose_route")
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = 0, end = Inf,
    cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
  )
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_bup <- nca_one(sim, "Cc")
nca_nor <- nca_one(sim, "Cc_norbup")

summarise_nca <- function(res, analyte) {
  as.data.frame(res) |>
    filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
    group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
    summarise(median = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
    mutate(analyte = analyte)
}
nca_tab <- bind_rows(summarise_nca(nca_bup, "buprenorphine"), summarise_nca(nca_nor, "norbuprenorphine"))
nca_tab |>
  select(analyte, treatment, cmax, tmax, aucinf.obs, half.life) |>
  rename(
    "Analyte" = analyte, "Route" = treatment, "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = aucinf.obs, "t1/2 (h)" = half.life
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median simulated NCA per route (200 virtual cats per route).")
```

## Comparison against published values

The paper reports one elimination half-life for buprenorphine across routes
(12.3 h, Table 3 'Current Study'). It is compared with the simulated
i.v. terminal half-life.

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~half.life,
  "IV", 12.3
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_bup,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published buprenorphine half-life. * differs by >20%.")

hl_iv <- as.data.frame(nca_bup) |>
  filter(treatment == "IV", PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  pull(PPORRES)
# The 24-72 h terminal slope sits close to beta.
stopifnot(abs(median(hl_iv, na.rm = TRUE) / 12.3 - 1) < 0.2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **First-pass norbuprenorphine dose.** The paper says FOTM is the 'parent
  and metabolite OTM bioavailability' and that the first-pass route was
  added to explain the higher norbuprenorphine exposure after buccal
  dosing, but it does not print the amount entering the gut-norbuprenorphine
  depot. The model applies FOTM to a buccal dose of the same amount entering
  that depot, which is the reading of 'parent and metabolite OTM
  bioavailability'. The individual data in S4 File support it: this reading
  reproduces the observed mean peak of buccal norbuprenorphine (4.4 vs 4.2
  ng/mL), while a first-pass input of 1% of the dose would give about 0.6
  ng/mL. The paper's sentence that the first-pass amount 'contributed to
  approximately 1% out of the value of FOTM (23.6%)' could not be reconciled
  with any structure the paper describes and is not used. With this reading
  the typical buccal norbuprenorphine curve peaks later (about 4 h vs 1 h)
  and stays about twice the observed mean from 4 to 48 h.
* **Norbuprenorphine formation is part of CL.** KaMet x central forms
  norbuprenorphine without an extra buprenorphine loss term, so CL is the
  total buprenorphine clearance. The paper calls CL the 'total body
  clearance', and its 12.3 h beta half-life is reproduced from CL, V1, CL2
  and V2 alone (11.7 h if KaMet were an additional loss). Formation is in
  mass units with no molecular-weight correction; nothing in the paper
  indicates a molar model.
* **Shape parameter of the time-dependent SC input.** S3 File states that
  gamma 'was approximated by the value of clearance'; the model uses the
  individual per-kg CL value read as hours.
* **CV of the inverse-Gaussian input.** The paper prints 'variance of the
  input time (CV) was 5.46'. The value is used as CV and squared in
  equation 5; this reproduces the paper's 0.08 h input peak (see Derived
  quantities).
* **IIV conversion.** All IIV percentages are converted with S3 File eq 3,
  including those of the logit-scale bioavailabilities FOTM, FSC and BIO.
  Parameters with 'IIV 0%' (CL2, Ke0, T0, Emax) and those with no estimated
  random effect (CL2Met, V2Met) carry no eta. The KaMet eta (19%) comes from
  the IV + SC fit made before the typical KaMet was fixed.
* **Residual error.** The paper names a proportional error for each analyte
  (common to the three routes) and an additive error for the thermal
  threshold, but does not report their magnitudes; all three are fixed to
  zero.
* **Inverse-Gaussian input with repeated doses.** The inverse-Gaussian term
  reads the amount and time of the most recent s.c. dose only, so it is
  exact for the single doses of the study but does not superpose earlier
  s.c. doses.
* **BIO complement.** The paper prints 1 - BIO as 89.1%; with BIO = 10.1% it
  is 89.9%, which is what the model uses.
* **Right censoring.** Thermal thresholds at the 55 degrees C cut-off were
  fitted as observed values; the paper's attempt at a censored-data
  likelihood did not converge, so the PD estimates are those of the
  uncensored fit.
* No correction notice for this article was found as of 2026-11-25.
